text:
Alex C: quick question — after I manually imported the payments service account into terraform in staging, `terraform plan` now wants to recreate it. I didn't touch the config, just imported. anyone seen this?
Jamie (infra): did you import using the same module address/provider alias we use in CI? sometimes provider differences make fields look changed.
Alex C: I ran `terraform import kubernetes_service_account.payments default/payments-sa` from the repo root, provider alias is k8s.cluster-staging (same as backend).
Maria S: can you paste the plan snippet showing the replacement? usually it's an annotation or field ordering.
Alex C: sure — plan shows: ```~ kubernetes_service_account.payments
  ~ metadata {
      ~ annotations = {
          - "kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration" = "..." -> null
        }
    }
  - id = "default/payments-sa" -> null
  + id = (known after apply)
  ~ lifecycle: replace triggers```
Maria S: that annotation is inserted by kubectl. We typically ignore annotations in the SA module with `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [metadata[0].annotations] }`.
Liam R: also check `terraform state show kubernetes_service_account.payments` — import sometimes doesn't capture nested lists the same way, making plan think it needs to replace.
Alex C: ran `terraform state show` — metadata.annotations is empty in state, cluster actually has the kubectl annotation. refresh didn't pick it up: `terraform refresh` returned no diffs.
Jamie (infra): odd. If state lacks the annotation but provider says present in cluster, refresh should detect that. Which provider version are you on? we bumped `hashicorp/kubernetes` recently.
Alex C: using provider 2.14.0 (same as repo lockfile).
Maria S: another failure mode: if the config address differs (module path changed) import attaches to a different address and state ends up inconsistent. run `terraform state list | grep payments` to confirm path.
Alex C: state list shows `module.k8s.module.payments.kubernetes_service_account.payments` — matches config.
Liam R: If it's just annotations and we don't want terraform to touch them, add the ignore_changes to the module, run plan — it should stop proposing replace. Adding ignore_changes is non-destructive.
Jamie (infra): procedure I'd do: 1) add `ignore_changes = [metadata[0].annotations]` in the SA resource in a small PR; 2) run `terraform plan -var-file=staging.tfvars` locally (or via a plan job); 3) if plan no longer wants replace, merge. If plan still wants replace, capture the `terraform state show` output and paste here.
Alex C: ok I'll open a tiny PR to add ignore_changes and run the staging plan.
Maria S: alternative if you prefer not to change module: `terraform state rm` then re-import after ensuring the provider sees the same fields, but that's more invasive.
Alex C: noted. One question: will adding ignore_changes mask real drift for other metadata keys we care about? we only want to ignore annotations.
Jamie (infra): yep, restrict to `metadata[0].annotations` only. we don't ignore labels or other metadata keys we manage.
deploy-bot: [notice] staging plan run queued (run id: 894) — will post results here.
Alex C: perfect — thanks. I'll push the PR and ping once the plan job completes. :thumbsup:
